productionConfigurationRationale.selectedServerConfiguration: 5-Fold ConvNeXt-Tiny Ensemble (fold0.pt..fold4.pt, 139,162,160 params) + V3 Logit Adjustment + Side-by-Side fold0.pt Telemetry + Parallel V6 10-Region Hessian Contours
productionConfigurationRationale.selectedBrowserClientFallback: v2-fold0-int8.onnx (33.86 MB INT8 quantized fold0.pt) for offline/client-only WebAssembly bandwidth efficiency
reasons: 1. Eliminates Single-Split Variance Outliers: On cheek_sagging and neck_sagging (where fold0.pt disagrees with the 5-fold consensus on 6/18 and 3/18 independent images respectively), fold0.pt alone flip-flops between Grade 2 (1.784) and Grade 1 (1.203) across two front-camera captures (android_01 vs. android_04) of the same 34F volunteer, whereas Folds 1..4 unanimously predict Grade 1 and the 5-Fold Ensemble remains stable at Grade 1 (1.067 vs. 1.032).

2. Surfaces Epistemic Inter-Fold Uncertainty: Reporting the 5-fold vote vector [f0, f1, f2, f3, f4] distinguishes unanimous 5/5 predictions (jawline_sagging 18/18 = 100% agreement, submental_sagging 18/18 = 100% agreement) from borderline split-vote cases (e.g., 3/5 or 2/5 consensus on cheek and neck).

3. Acceptable Workstation Latency & RAM Cost: 5-Fold CPU inference averages ~705 ms (vs. ~147 ms for fold0.pt) and requires 530.86 MB of FP32 weight tensors in RAM (+424.69 MB over fold0.pt), well within local workstation capacity.

4. No Claim of Validated Clinical Superiority: In accordance with clinical governance, this configuration is chosen for software variance reduction and uncertainty transparency, NOT claimed clinical superiority, pending dual-physician blinded grading on consented real patients.
